ranked_facts.concept_key: Nodular Proliferations of Thick Collagen Fibers
ranked_facts.why: The presence of nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles is more characteristic of Eosinophilic Fasciitis than Systemic Sclerosis-related Cutaneous Fibrosis, as the latter typically presents with a more homogeneous pattern of collagen deposition.

The absence of appreciable skin tightening in the affected areas is more consistent with Eosinophilic Fasciitis, which typically does not involve significant skin tightening, in contrast to Systemic Sclerosis-related Cutaneous Fibrosis and Morphea, where skin tightening is a hallmark feature.
